subject: Discovery recap & procurement framing - NovaSys Solutions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@novasys.com>, Tom Becker <tom.becker@novasys.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & procurement framing - NovaSys Solutions

Hi Samantha and Tom —

Thanks for your time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into procurement: 

Summary of what we heard (pain & goals)
- Latency variability on your inference endpoints during daytime spikes causing degraded UX for power users (esp. reports generation).
- Current stack: in-house model serving built on k8s + batch workers; using mixed GPU fleet (older cards) with variable autoscaling.
- Primary goal: consistent sub-300ms tail latency for key flows, reduce per-token cost by ~30% vs today, and get stronger observability/tracing for regressions.

Success criteria (how you’ll evaluate a POC)
- Demonstrable 99th percentile latency <300ms on representative workload (our runner against your production-like traces).
- Token cost reduction target (baseline + 30% reduction or better).
- Integration with your KMS and audit log export for compliance review.
- Team signoff from Infra + ML Platform + Security.

Procurement framing / decision process (as discussed)
- Timeline: NovaSys roadmap aims to select a vendor in August, procurement/contracting to complete by end of September.
- Key stakeholders:
  - Samantha Liu (Technical Buyer / ML Platform)
  - Tom Becker (Procurement / Vendor Evaluation)
  - Maya Ortiz (CISO, security ok-to-proceed) — we understand security will request SOC2 + audit evidence.
- Initial commercial guardrails you mentioned:
  - Preference for a limited pilot (4–8 week POC) with a capped spend (~$25k–$50k) and clear success metrics before committing to reserved capacity.
  - Need indicative pricing bands for a POC + example committed tier options so Procurement can build a redline plan.

Proposed next steps
1) We’ll share a one-pager + draft POC SOW we can use to align internal stakeholders (attached).
2) Rishi will propose a POC sizing and test plan (what traces we need, expected hardware) — target end of week.
3) Schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive with your ML Platform + Security to cover integration and audit artifacts (can do Wed/Thu next week).
4) Intro to our legal/compliance contacts once NovaSys confirms timeline + procurement contact (Tom) — we can pre-share standard contract terms and a non-prod Data Processing Addendum.

Attachments: Redwood_OnePager.pdf, Initial_POC_SOW_Draft_v1.docx (links above).

If this aligns, I’ll follow up with Rishi’s POC plan and propose two slots for the technical deep-dive.

Thanks again —
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from Procurement: 

- The $25k–$50k cap for a pilot is in the ballpark we expected. Procurement will want indicative pricing bands: PoC (capped spend) vs committed reserved capacity (monthly committed). Can you provide a high-level example (range) per concurrency tier?
- We need to ensure any PII/production traces used for the PoC are covered by a data handling agreement; what does Redwood require to run traces?
- Timeline: August decision is tight but doable; Procurement will need 2–3 weeks to complete vendor assessments after a favorable POC.

Action items on our side: I’ll confirm the internal stakeholders list and loop in our legal lead if the SOW contains anything atypical.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & procurement framing - NovaSys Solutions

Marissa — nice capture. A few internal notes I think we should include when we send the POC plan to NovaSys: 

- POC sizing suggestions:
  - Run 1: representative 2-hour peak replay (we ask for production traces or synthetic trace that matches peak QPS).
  - HW: 2x A100 equivalent GPUs for the runner (we can run on CPU/GPU mix depending on model), estimated cost for 4–6 weeks within their $25k–$50k cap if we provide a focused test load.
- Success metrics: 99th pctl latency <300ms, token cost reduction >=25% (we’ll baseline to their provided trace).
- Security/compliance: we can run the POC in a customer-provided VPC if they prefer; otherwise Redwood will provide dedicated tenant and mask PII in traces. We will provide SOC2 report and our standard DPA; legal typically asks for a 30–60 day review for standard SOWs.
- Commercial guardrail examples (to help Tom):
  - PoC: timeboxed 4–8 weeks, flat capped spend (example: $35k), limited to test traffic and non-prod SLAs.
  - Transition to Reserved: monthly committed capacity discounts (we can propose X% discount on per-token/unit pricing for 6/12 month commitments).

I’ll draft a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that enumerates milestones, owners, and acceptance criteria. Marissa — want me to send the MAP + detailed POC plan directly to Samantha and Tom, or should it come from you?

Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
